basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 20.' and it opens '(Cap. XXXIV.—Vers. 20.) Et venit Emor et Sichem filius ejus ad portam civitatis suae, et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XXXIV.—Vers. 20.) Et venit Emor et Sichem filius ejus ad portam civitatis suae, et locuti sunt ad viros civitatis dicentes, viri isti pacifici nobis [Al. nobiscum] sunt. Ubi nunc Septuaginta Interpretes pacificos transtulerunt, Aquila interpretatus est, ἀπηρτισμένους, id est, consummatos atque perfectos, pro quo in Hebraeo legitur (שלמים) SALAMIM. Ex quo perspicuum est, verum esse illud quod supra de Salem diximus.
